27/G.goal: Explain how the behavior of light and the physiology of the human eye shape visual perception and inform VR headset design, rendering, camera placement, and tracking.
27/G.achieves: It provides the foundational human-factors knowledge needed to understand and later implement XR systems with confidence.

27/O1.goal: Explain why visual perception, light propagation, and lenses are important for VR headset design, virtual world rendering, camera placement, and tracking.
27/O1.achieves: It connects the lecture’s optical and perceptual concepts to concrete XR system design and implementation issues.

27/O2.goal: Describe how the photon, wave, and ray models of light, surface interaction, and reflected light intensity determine perceived color.
27/O2.achieves: It gives the learner an optical basis for understanding rendering, display, and color representation in XR systems.

27/O3.goal: Describe how human eye anatomy, visible light, and photoreceptor function explain photopic and scotopic vision, central and peripheral vision, and the blind spot.
27/O3.achieves: It lets the learner understand the visual capabilities and limitations that XR displays and immersive experiences must account for.
